body: Fundsmith Equity launched 1 Nov 2010. To 31 Dec 2025: +612.9% cumulative, 13.8% annualised vs MSCI World +467.6% / 12.1% (fund's annual letter). But 2025 returned only +0.8% vs +12.8% for MSCI World - the fifth consecutive calendar year of underperformance (2021-2025) and the weakest year since inception; the since-inception annualised figure fell from 14.8% at end-2024. Process: three rules - buy good companies (high ROCE, high gross margins, cash conversion, low leverage, resilient demand, no banks or heavy cyclicals), don't overpay (free-cash-flow yield vs bonds), do nothing (very low turnover). ~25-30 holdings. Structural edge: low-fee, transparent fund with a long-horizon UK retail base. Smith blamed 2025 on index concentration in a few mega-caps, passive flows and dollar weakness. Mistakes: owning quality at 30-40x earnings left the fund exposed to de-rating (e.g., Novo Nordisk's 2024-25 collapse; earlier PayPal exit; unverified magnitudes). Lesson: even a sound quality process can lag for five years when style or valuation turns; 'don't overpay' is the rule most often broken. Copyable for Indians: the quality checklist maps well to India's consumer/financial compounders, but valuation discipline (FCF yield vs 10-year G-sec) matters most when quality trades at 60-80x.
title: Terry Smith - Fundsmith quality: buy good companies, don't overpay, do nothing
